How do you care for lucky bamboo in the UAE?

Lucky bamboo (Dracaena sanderiana) is a tropical dracaena, not a true bamboo, that grows in water or soil. For lucky bamboo care, give it bright, indirect light away from direct sun and keep the roots under clean, chlorine-free water, changed weekly (Clemson Extension). In UAE homes, keep it out of AC draughts and switch to filtered or distilled water if the leaf tips brown.

Dracaena sanderiana (sometimes sold as Dracaena braunii, a separate species) · Also called Ribbon plant, Friendship bamboo, Chinese water bamboo, Water bamboo, خيزران الحظ

Lucky Bamboo quick facts

What it isA tropical dracaena from Central Africa, not a true bamboo
LightBright, indirect light. Direct sun turns the leaves brown.
In waterWater over the roots and at least 2.5 cm of stem; change it weekly (Clemson Extension).
In soilWell-drained potting soil; water when the top 2.5 cm is dry (Clemson Extension).
Water typeChlorine-free; filtered or distilled water if tips brown. Dracaenas are sensitive to fluoride.
Temperature21–27 °C is ideal indoors; keep it above about 15 °C at all times (UF/IFAS Extension).
FeedingIn water: liquid houseplant fertiliser at a quarter strength, every other month (Clemson Extension).
PetsToxic to cats and dogs (ASPCA)
GrowthSlow. Rarely flowers indoors.

Is a lucky bamboo right for you?

A good fit if

  • You want a plant that grows in a vase of water, with no soil to manage.
  • Your room has bright, indirect light but no direct sun on the plant.
  • You want a small, slow-growing plant for a desk, a shelf or a reception counter.
  • You want a plant to give as a gift: lucky bamboo is often given for celebrations.

Think twice if

  • A cat or a dog in your home chews plants: lucky bamboo is toxic to them.
  • You will not change the water regularly or keep the water line over the roots.
  • The only place for it is in direct sun or in the stream of an AC vent.

How much light does lucky bamboo need?

A lucky bamboo plant needs bright, indirect light, such as near an east- or north-facing window (Clemson Extension). Direct sunlight damages lucky bamboo leaves and turns them brown.

In the UAE, the main light risk for lucky bamboo is afternoon sun through west- or south-facing glass. Move the plant back from that window or filter the sun with a sheer curtain. Lucky bamboo also tolerates shade, so a bright room away from the window is a better place than a sunny sill.

Shop: Lucky Bamboo Stick In Glass Vase With Black Stones

How do you grow lucky bamboo in water, and how often should you change it?

Keep enough water in a lucky bamboo vase to cover the roots and at least one inch (2.5 cm) of each stem (Clemson Extension), and change the water weekly. Both Clemson Extension and NC State Extension give that weekly change; NC State says it also stops mosquitoes breeding in the vase.

The water line in a lucky bamboo vase, not the date, tells you when to top up: look at the vase, and when the roots are no longer under water, add fresh water. Evaporation needs energy from the sun and the air (NOAA), so the level falls sooner in a warm, bright spot than in a cool AC room.

Pebbles or glass stones at the bottom of the vase hold the lucky bamboo stalks upright (Clemson Extension). NC State Extension adds that pebbles give the roots room and add weight, so the vase does not tip.

  1. Lift the stalks out and hold them together.
  2. Pour away the old water and rinse the vase and the pebbles.
  3. Put the pebbles back and stand the stalks on them.
  4. Fill with fresh, chlorine-free water until the roots and at least 2.5 cm of stem are under water (Clemson Extension).

Shop: Pebble Stones, Lucky Bamboo Stick- Dracaena Sanderiana

Should you use tap water or filtered water for lucky bamboo?

Use chlorine-free water for lucky bamboo (NC State Extension). Dracaenas are sensitive to fluoride: the Oregon State University plant disease handbook lists most dracaena species and cultivars as sensitive to fluoride (it does not name lucky bamboo), and Ask Extension answers from Ohio State and Michigan State say lucky bamboo is sensitive to chlorine and fluoride.

UAE tap water is desalinated and then remineralised, and its mineral content varies by area and building. High fluoride, boron or salts make dracaena leaf tips and edges turn yellow or brown, and those damaged leaves do not recover (UF/IFAS Extension). If the tips brown or a white crust forms on the vase or pebbles, switch to filtered (reverse osmosis) or distilled water. For lucky bamboo, a University of Maryland Extension answer suggests distilled water, or tap water that has stood for a day.

Can lucky bamboo grow in soil?

Yes. Plant lucky bamboo in a well-drained potting soil for indoor or tropical plants, and water when the top inch (2.5 cm) of soil is dry (Clemson Extension). Do not leave water standing in the saucer under the pot. Stake tall lucky bamboo stems until the roots anchor into the soil (Clemson Extension).

Lucky bamboo in soil needs less work than lucky bamboo in water, because there is no water to change (Michigan State University Extension answer). In soil, overwatering is the main risk: NC State Extension says too much water turns the leaves yellow and rots the stems.

Shop: Universal Potting Soil – Holland

What temperature does lucky bamboo need under AC?

Lucky bamboo grows best at normal room temperature. UF/IFAS Extension gives 21–27 °C (70–80 °F) as the most suitable indoor range for dracaenas and says to avoid draughts.

Cold harms lucky bamboo. UF/IFAS Extension says to keep dracaenas above about 15 °C (60 °F) at all times, because chilling injury causes slimy, dead spots on the leaves and heavy leaf drop.

Keep lucky bamboo out of the direct stream of an AC vent. With the AC on, hold your hand next to the leaves: if you feel the air moving, move the plant or turn the louvres away from it.

Does lucky bamboo need fertiliser?

Lucky bamboo needs very little fertiliser. For lucky bamboo in water, Clemson Extension advises a liquid houseplant fertiliser at a quarter of the label rate, every other month. For lucky bamboo in soil, Clemson Extension advises a houseplant fertiliser monthly in the growing season.

Too much fertiliser adds salts, and UF/IFAS Extension lists high soluble salts as a cause of dracaena leaf tips turning yellow or brown. When in doubt, feed less.

How do you propagate lucky bamboo?

Lucky bamboo grows from stem cuttings (NC State Extension). Clemson Extension says new roots usually form within 2 to 3 weeks in water. A cut lucky bamboo stalk sends out new leaves at the node below the cut (Ohio State University Extension answer).

  1. Cut a shoot of new growth off the main stem with clean scissors.
  2. Remove the lowest leaves from the shoot.
  3. Stand the shoot in clean, chlorine-free water in bright, indirect light.
  4. Keep the cut end under water and change the water as for the main plant until roots form.

What should you do in the first week after your lucky bamboo arrives?

New lucky bamboo needs a stable spot and clean water. The main risks in the first week are direct sun and a cold draught.

  1. Put the vase in bright, indirect light, away from direct sun and from AC vents.
  2. Check that the water covers the roots and at least 2.5 cm of each stem (Clemson Extension). Top it up with chlorine-free water if it does not.
  3. Do not repot or feed it yet: UF/IFAS Extension advises no repotting or fertiliser for about four weeks after dracaenas are placed indoors.

How does lucky bamboo care change through the UAE year?

Summer May–Sep

Keep lucky bamboo indoors in bright, indirect light, which NC State Extension describes as suitable all year. The sources describe it outdoors only in shade or partial shade in summer, and neither gives advice for heat like a Dubai summer, when days reach about 41–42 °C and nights stay warm. Keep the vase out of sun through west- or south-facing glass. Water evaporates faster in a warm room, so look at the water line more often.

Autumn Oct–Nov

The outdoor gardening season starts in October, but lucky bamboo stays in its indoor spot. Keep the weekly water change that Clemson and NC State Extension advise, and the same bright, indirect spot.

Winter Dec–Feb

Coastal winter nights (lows of about 14–16 °C) come close to the chilling limit, so keep lucky bamboo away from cold glass and open doors. Inland (Al Ain, desert areas, the mountains) and in Riyadh or Kuwait, nights get much colder: keep lucky bamboo indoors and away from cold windows and doors, above about 15 °C (UF/IFAS Extension).

Spring Mar–Apr

Lucky bamboo in soil can have its monthly feed in the growing season (Clemson Extension). If the sun starts to reach the plant through the window, move it back: direct sun turns the leaves brown (Clemson Extension).

Why are my lucky bamboo leaves turning yellow?

Yellow lucky bamboo leaves usually come from too much light or from the water. Direct sun scorches the leaves; chlorine and fluoride in tap water cause yellow and brown leaves and leaf drop; in soil, too much water turns the leaves yellow. Lower leaves also age and die naturally.

How to tell: Yellow leaves on the sunny side, brown tips with the yellowing, or soil that stays wet.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the plant out of direct sun into bright, indirect light.
  2. Change the water and use filtered or distilled water from now on.
  3. In soil, let the top 2.5 cm dry before you water again (Clemson Extension), and empty the saucer.
  4. Cut off fully yellow leaves with clean, sterilised scissors.

Why are the leaf tips on my lucky bamboo turning brown?

Brown tips on lucky bamboo usually come from fluoride, boron or salts in the water or from too much fertiliser. UF/IFAS Extension says these damaged leaves do not recover. Direct sun and low humidity can also brown the tips.

How to tell: Brown tips or edges, sometimes with a white crust on the vase, the pebbles or the pot rim.

How to fix it:

  1. Change the water and rinse the vase and pebbles.
  2. Switch to filtered (reverse osmosis) or distilled water.
  3. Feed less, and only at a quarter of the label rate in water (Clemson Extension).
  4. Move the plant out of direct sun and away from AC vents.
  5. Trim the brown tips with clean scissors if you like. The damaged parts do not recover (UF/IFAS Extension).

Why is my lucky bamboo stalk turning yellow, brown or soft?

A lucky bamboo stalk that turns soft has a disease or rot, and that part does not recover. A firm stalk that changes colour can simply be getting woody as it matures. Ohio State University Extension advises rooting a healthy top on its own, so a disease does not spread to the other stalks.

How to tell: A soft or mushy area on the stalk (rot), or a firm area that only changes colour (often ageing).

How to fix it:

  1. Take the soft stalk out of the vase straight away.
  2. If the top of the stalk is still firm and green, cut it off above the soft part with clean scissors.
  3. Root that top on its own in fresh water, not in the vase with the other stalks.
  4. Throw away the soft part.
  5. Rinse the vase and pebbles and refill the vase with fresh, chlorine-free water.

What are the white cotton spots or fine webs on my lucky bamboo?

White cotton or fine webs on lucky bamboo are signs of sap-sucking pests. NC State Extension lists mealybugs, mites and scale, and Clemson Extension lists spider mites, mealybugs and aphids.

How to tell: White fluff on the leaves or stalks, or fine webs under the leaves.

How to fix it:

  1. Keep the plant away from your other plants until the pests are gone.
  2. Remove the pests by hand or rinse the leaves under running water.
  3. Spray both sides of the leaves with neem oil or insecticidal soap, as the label says.
  4. Check the plant again after each spray and repeat while you still find pests.

Helps: Neem Shield – Herbal Pesticide

Why does my lucky bamboo have slimy spots and dropped leaves after a cold night?

Slimy, dead spots and heavy leaf drop on lucky bamboo are signs of chilling injury, which UF/IFAS Extension links to temperatures below about 15 °C (60 °F). In the UAE the risk is highest on inland and GCC winter nights, near a cold window or an open door.

How to tell: Spots that look wet or slimy, then turn dark, and many leaves dropping at once.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the plant to a warmer spot, away from AC vents and cold glass.
  2. Cut off the damaged leaves with clean scissors.
  3. Keep the water change and light as normal and let new leaves grow.

What mistakes kill a lucky bamboo?

A sunny windowsillBright, indirect light. Direct sun turns lucky bamboo leaves brown.
A spot under an AC ventKeep the plant out of the direct stream of air. Use the hand test with the AC on.
Full-strength fertiliser in the vaseA liquid houseplant fertiliser at a quarter of the label rate, every other month (Clemson Extension).

Lucky Bamboo myths and facts

MythFact
Lucky bamboo is a type of bamboo.Lucky bamboo is not a bamboo at all. It is Dracaena sanderiana, a tropical shrub from Central Africa in the asparagus family.
Lucky bamboo in water needs no care.Lucky bamboo in water needs clean, chlorine-free water that covers the roots, changed weekly (Clemson Extension).
Lucky bamboo grows in spirals by itself.Spiral and braided lucky bamboo stalks are trained into those shapes by the grower (NC State Extension).
Lucky bamboo needs a lot of sun, like garden bamboo.Lucky bamboo needs bright, indirect light. Direct sun damages its leaves.

Is a lucky bamboo safe for cats and dogs?

No. The ASPCA lists ribbon plant (Dracaena species), a common name of lucky bamboo, as toxic to cats and dogs. The plant contains saponins, which can cause vomiting (sometimes with blood), depression, loss of appetite and drooling, and dilated pupils in cats. NC State Extension adds that people should not eat it and that the sap can irritate the skin. Keep lucky bamboo out of reach of pets and young children.

If your pet chewed it: Call your vet or a 24-hour animal emergency clinic straight away and tell them the plant name. Do not wait for symptoms.

Lucky Bamboo FAQs

What does the number of lucky bamboo stalks mean?

Lucky bamboo is a symbolic plant in Chinese culture and a popular gift for celebrations such as Chinese New Year. In that tradition, Clemson Extension says one stalk stands for good fortune, two for love, three for happiness, five for health and six for prosperity, and it leaves out four, which is not considered lucky. These are traditional meanings, not something the plant does.

Is lucky bamboo better in water or in soil?

Lucky bamboo grows in both. In water it needs clean, chlorine-free water changed weekly (Clemson Extension); in well-drained soil there is no water to change, so it needs less work (Michigan State University Extension answer). In soil, the main risk is overwatering.

Is lucky bamboo a real bamboo?

Lucky bamboo is not a real bamboo. It is Dracaena sanderiana, a tropical shrub from Central Africa that looks like bamboo when its lower leaves are removed (Clemson Extension). Lucky bamboo is in the asparagus family (NC State Extension).

Will lucky bamboo grow new leaves if I cut the top off?

Yes. A cut lucky bamboo stalk sends out new leaves at the node below the cut (Ohio State University Extension answer). You can root the cut top in water as a new plant.

How tall does lucky bamboo grow?

Lucky bamboo grows slowly. UF/IFAS Extension says the stems never become strong enough to stay upright beyond about 60–90 cm (2–3 feet), so tall stems need support. Indoors, lucky bamboo rarely flowers (NC State Extension).

Can lucky bamboo grow outdoors in the UAE?

Keep lucky bamboo indoors in the UAE. NC State Extension describes it indoors in bright, indirect light all year, and outdoors only in partial shade in summer. Clemson Extension says to bring it in before nights fall below 18 °C (65 °F). Neither source gives advice for UAE summer heat, and inland winter nights can fall below the 15 °C chilling limit (UF/IFAS Extension).

Is lucky bamboo safe for children?

Lucky bamboo should not be eaten. NC State Extension lists its poison severity as low, says people should not eat it and says the sap can irritate the skin. Keep it out of reach of young children, and wash your hands after you cut stalks.
